# ai-model-catalogue — the contract for writing a consumer

> Which AI model each feature calls, what each one costs, and when it retires.
> One Ed25519-signed file, fetched by every deployment, verified against a
> public key compiled into the product. GitHub and the CDN are delivery, not
> authority: neither is trusted, and neither needs to be.

If you are writing or changing code that reads this catalogue, this file is the
contract. `README.md` is for whoever publishes it. `catalogue.schema.json` is
the shape, and `build.mjs` enforces it before signing, so the two cannot drift.

## What is fetched

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/surapas3022/ai-model-catalogue/config.stable.json
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/surapas3022/ai-model-catalogue/config.canary.json
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/surapas3022/ai-model-catalogue/lineup.stable.json
```

Fetch `config.<your channel>.json` and nothing else, unless you price usage. It
carries both the chains and a rate for every model it can reach, so it is
complete on its own.

`lineup.stable.json` is the second catalogue: same envelope, same key, same
checks, every model the provider publishes with its rate, and no routing
opinion. Fetch it as well when your cost report meets model ids `config` does
not describe, and read prices from it. **Never take a chain from it.** Its
`purposes` holds one copy of what `config` already routes to, because the format
requires the field, and following it would freeze routing at the day the lineup
was written.

The file is an envelope, not the catalogue:

```json
{ "payload": "<the catalogue, as a JSON string>", "sig": "<base64>" }
```

`payload` is a string on purpose. The signature covers exact bytes, and parsing
then re-serialising an object changes key order, which turns a perfectly valid
catalogue into one that fails to verify with nothing to show why. Verify the
bytes you received. Never verify a re-serialised object.

```js
crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(payload, "utf8"), PUBLIC_KEY_PEM, Buffer.from(sig, "base64"))
```

## Do and do not

- DO compile the public key into the build. Fetching it defeats the signature
  entirely: whoever served you a forged catalogue would serve the key for it.
- DO keep the last catalogue that verified, and fall back to it.
- DO keep a hardcoded chain of model ids in the product as a last resort, below
  the cached copy. A deployment whose catalogue is unreadable must keep
  answering customers, not stop.
- DO treat every rejection as the same event: keep using what you already have,
  and say so somewhere an operator will see.
- DO NOT throw out of the adopt path. There is one answer to every failure.
- DO NOT read `catalogue.src.json` at runtime. It is unsigned, it carries
  `_comment` keys that never reach the wire, and it is for maintainers.
- DO NOT let an unverified payload reach any other code, including for logging.
- DO NOT pin `@latest`. Use the plain path, or `@<tag>` when you need a file
  that will never move.

## After the signature verifies

In order, and all of them before the catalogue is adopted:

1. `JSON.parse(payload)`.
2. Reject if `version` is not an integer, or is not greater than the version you
   already hold. A stale copy sitting in a CDN edge must never walk a deployment
   backwards. First run: compare against 0.
3. Reject if `minClientVersion` is greater than this build's `CLIENT_VERSION`.
   An old build reading a new file and silently missing the part that mattered
   is worse than an old build that kept working.
4. Reject if `channel` is not the channel this build was generated for. A
   canary file reaching a stable build is a mis-deploy, not an upgrade.
5. Reject if `purposes.default` is missing or empty.
6. Reject if any chain names a model id that `models` does not describe. The
   cost of not checking is not a crash: it is a cost report that falls back to
   `fallbackPrice` and reads plausibly while being wrong.

## Choosing a model

`purposes` maps a feature id to an ordered chain of model ids. The keys are the
exact strings the product already passes at its call sites, so that the model
map and the cost report name things the same way.

- A feature with no key here falls to `purposes.default`. Adding a feature to
  the product before adding it here is therefore safe.
- Walk the chain in order. Take the first model that is answering.
- `retiresOn` is the date the provider stops answering, or null.

## Prices

`models.<id>.price` is `{ input, cachedInput, output }` in USD per 1,000,000
tokens. Note the nesting: the price is an object under `price`, not three fields
on the model.

```
usd = inputTokens / 1e6 * price.input
    + cachedInputTokens / 1e6 * price.cachedInput
    + outputTokens / 1e6 * price.output
thb = usd * usdToThb
```

`usdToThb` is applied at the single edge where a USD rate becomes a baht figure.
A model id with no entry in `models` uses `fallbackPrice`, which exists so that
an unrecognised model does not report as free. A model listed in this catalogue
always has its own price: `build.mjs` refuses to sign one that does not.

## Embeddings are not a chain

`kb-embed-index` and `kb-embed-query` name exactly one model each, and
`build.mjs` refuses more. A fallback there would write a second model's vectors
into the same table that retrieval reads without filtering by model, and the
result is not worse search, it is meaningless search, with nothing surfacing as
an error.

An embedding model carries `embedding: true` and `dim`. `dim` is part of the
model's identity rather than a setting: vectors already stored were written at
that width, and cosine against a different width means nothing. A consumer that
already holds vectors should treat what is on disk as winning over what the
catalogue says, and raise an alert rather than silently re-pointing.

## The catalogue object

| field | |
|---|---|
| `version` | integer, only ever goes up |
| `channel` | `stable` or `canary`, stamped inside the payload |
| `minClientVersion` | integer; above your `CLIENT_VERSION` means ignore the file |
| `publishedAt` | ISO 8601, operator-facing only |
| `notes` | optional, operator-facing only |
| `usdToThb` | positive number |
| `models` | model id to `{ price, vision, embedding?, dim?, status, retiresOn }` |
| `purposes` | feature id to an ordered array of model ids; `default` required |
| `fallbackPrice` | `{ input, cachedInput, output }` |

`status` is `ga`, `preview`, `deprecated` or `retired`. `retired` means no chain
may name it, which `build.mjs` enforces; `deprecated` is a warning and nothing
more. `vision` says the model can be handed an image, and `build.mjs` refuses to
sign an image-reading chain that falls to a model without it.

## Failure table

| what happened | what the consumer does |
|---|---|
| fetch failed | keep the cached catalogue |
| not a `{ payload, sig }` pair | keep the cached catalogue |
| signature does not verify | keep the cached catalogue; never parse the payload |
| version not newer | keep the cached catalogue; this is the normal no-op |
| `minClientVersion` too high | keep the cached catalogue; the build needs updating |
| catalogue malformed | fall to the hardcoded chain, and alert |
| every model in a chain retired | fall to `default`, then to the hardcoded chain |
